en-GB.codex_unit_airtrooper_cherrystone_lore_t: It's hard to imagine now, but in days of old, braised Flamingo was a delicacy among the Cherrystone nobility. Thankfully, the kingdom has long ended this barbarous practice, and instead raises the birds as beasts of war.
en-GB.codex_unit_airtrooper_critical_text: Critical Hit when the Target is sandwiched between two Air Troopers.
en-GB.codex_unit_airtrooper_faahri_lore_text:
Fairfowl are not native to our mountains, nor to the peoples of the foothills. Nevertheless, they have proven themselves indispensable for longer journeys with difficult terrain, as feline mounts are practically useless after a few hours of labour.

In the Fairfowl’s native lands, legends tell of a great warrior who favoured the birds, and oft rode them into battle. In our experience, the Fairfowl more than hold their own in combat. As such, their riders are unarmed, focusing on training the fowl and opening doors for them when necessary. (Fairfowl do not typically possess hands or fingers.)
en-GB.codex_unit_airtrooper_felheim_lore_text: A bird of prey that feasts upon the decaying flesh of the dead, the Giant Vulture is widely considered "the most Felheim thing imaginable," and has been unanimously voted as the country's official bird every year since the rankings began.
en-GB.codex_unit_airtrooper_floran_lore_text:
The Toumingo may *look* silly, awkward and confused. But they are also in a constant state of terror and horrified to be alive.

Legend tells of a Toumingo with wings of flame, a terrifying beast capable of burning down whole forests and birthing them anew.
en-GB.codex_unit_airtrooper_heavensong_lore_te:
Empress Tenri's mother, the late Empress-consort, belonged to the Order of the Golden Crane. Long has the order been the direct protectors of the royal family; however, before her majesty, none of the Order had ever been part of the royal family itself. The union of the Crane and the Heavens was an auspicious day. Would that the joy lasted eternal.

It is said that the founding members of the Golden Crane lineage saved the Heavensong Empire from annihilation--before it was an Empire and even before it was called Heavensong. An ancient folk tune references (but does not itself contain) a "Song of Heaven" that protected the survivors of an ancient doomed kingdom from demise.
en-GB.codex_unit_archer_cherrystone_lore_text: The Ranger is Cherrystone's Archer unit. Cherrystone Rangers are almost impossibly nimble, able to nock and loose an arrow in the blink of an eye. It is a long-held tradition for Rangers to meet at eventide on the brink of the summer solstice and thank the winds for guiding their arrows. This tradition calls, of course, for the hearty consumption of cinnamon ale whilst leaping fully clothed and half-witted into the river Aldor.
en-GB.codex_unit_archer_critical_text:
▲ Hits units up to 3 tiles away. 
▲ Can strike Air and Naval units.
▲ Can shoot over Wall tiles. 
▽ Protect Archers from hostile
  melee units! 

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when stationary.
en-GB.codex_unit_archer_faahri_lore_text:
Archery serves little practical use for those who dwell within the halls and mines of the mountains. It is, however, a popular and relaxing pastime for Faahri who live in the fields and forests of the mountain range. 

For foreigners not familiar with Faahri pastimes, the word "relaxing" here means "extremely intense and competitive." 

Faahri archery competitions are triannual affairs with dozens of categories for both individual and team events.
en-GB.codex_unit_archer_felheim_lore_text: The Dreadbow is Felheim's Archer unit. They fashion arrowheads from their own ribs, believing this gives them some control over their flight - a process that essentially assigns each undead archer an expiry date. Should a Dreadbow survive long enough that all of their ribs are gone, they retire from battle, spending the rest of their undeath at Silentstone in east Felheim.
en-GB.codex_unit_archer_floran_lore_text: The Shooter is the Floran Archer unit. Floran Shooters make up for their crude bone bows with their absolute mastery of archery, an art they practise in their hunts along the River Bani, which flows into the Floran Lands via the West Sea. A Shooter cares little for the size or ferocity of its prey, instead coveting the most elusive and agile foes, and attains a remarkable degree of accuracy despite poorly weighted arrows.
en-GB.codex_unit_archer_heavensong_lore_text:
The Hawkbow is Heavensong's Archer unit. They practise their Archery high on the Glittering Peaks in southern Heavensong with bows that are nothing short of modern marvels. Effortless to draw and ultra-lightweight, they fire arrows with tips that unfold mid-flight to maximise both distance and deadliness.

The Hawkbow wear the mask of their avian namesake as a mark of their keen eye and affinity with the wind.
en-GB.codex_unit_archer_pirates_lore_text:
Bill’s an odd fellow. All of Tealbeard’s crew are, really. They joke and laugh as if they’ve not just made enemies of the two most powerful nations in Aurania. They put their lives at risk for people they didn’t know about ‘til yesterday. 

“Ain’t no honour among thieves,” Bill told me recently. “But there’s solidarity amongst subjugated classes of peoples against the tyranny of an oppressive colonial force.”

He has offered me some reading material from an Auranian philosopher who “Has loads of good ideas, mate!” I haven’t the time to read it, but the thought was nice.
en-GB.codex_unit_ballista_cherrystone_lore_tex: Each Ballista is manned and maintained by a skilled Bowman. The Bowman will grow to appreciate the eccentricities of his or her particular Ballista, compensating for its shortcomings and leaning into its strengths. Should the machine be damaged in battle, the Bowman will carefully relearn the idiosyncrasies of his newly mended charge.
en-GB.codex_unit_ballista_critical_text:
▲ Anti-Air unit with a large 
  attack range.
▽ Less powerful vs. ground units.
▽ Can’t move and attack on the
  same turn. 

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when Target is at min. 
    attack range.
en-GB.codex_unit_ballista_faahri_lore_text: Second-rate projectile-motion calculators can save face somewhat by becoming ballista engineers; however, they aren't fooling anyone. The higher speed and weight of this launcher's projectile makes path calculation a task an infant could do.
en-GB.codex_unit_ballista_felheim_lore_text:
Felheim soldiers take a quantity over quality approach to the operation of Ballistas, learning to reload and fire them with blinding speed and miserable inaccuracy (this actually works better than you'd think).

Felheim's Ballistas shoot dread bolts. These are exactly the same as normal bolts, but with the word 'dread' attached.
en-GB.codex_unit_ballista_floran_lore_text: The Floran Ballista is a crude device, constructed from wood, bone and springy vines. Despite this, the Florans' honed hunting instincts and keen eyes render it a powerful addition to their arsenal. It fires a vicious bolt made entirely of jagged bone. The bolt is razor-sharp, light-weight and durable, able to cover dramatic distances and pierce the strongest armour.
en-GB.codex_unit_ballista_heavensong_lore_text: With a complex system of internal pulleys and ropes, Heavensong's Ballistas are able to loose a bolt that can attain frightening flight speed, providing it with incredible accuracy and power. The front wheels are made of tungsten, delivering enough weight to keep the Ballista grounded despite enormous recoil.
en-GB.codex_unit_ballista_pirates_lore_text:
Dawn was breaking, and the ship cabin’s air smelled of ash. 

“I wish we had noodles,” Samyr thought as he calmly stepped over bodies and broken bits of the ship. He unlocked the ship’s armoury, retrieved a few ballista bolts, and brushed off the slime residue before carrying them up to the deck.

As the Heavensong dragon soared overhead, Samyr realized he'd forgotten to check out the ballista from the ship's library--captain's new rules. Luckily, it was a Thursday. Samyr figured he could get more accuracy on the bolt if they had better rapport, so he rocked it in his arms and told it how much he loved being it's dad. 

The bolt let out a terrifying human scream that woke Samyr from his slumber. Now, the only damage to the ship was the ballista bolt he'd just shot through the main sail.

From the upper deck, the captain groans. 

“Sleepwalking *again*?”
en-GB.codex_unit_balloon_cherrystone_lore_text: Cherrystone Balloons are woven from a silk produced by silkworms found on the western edge of the Gloomwoods. Powered by a particularly potent Alchemist's brew, they are capable of transporting heavy cargo and staying aloft almost indefinitely. Once in a while, the Balloon's pilot will add iron filings to the brew to ensure it continues to bubble. No one questions why this works for fear it may stop.
en-GB.codex_unit_balloon_critical_text:
▲ Transports up to two of any
  footsoldier, dog, or 
  Air Trooper
▽ When this unit is defeated,
  any unit it carries is lost.
▲ Useful for reaching inaccessible
  areas - and for making
  hasty retreats. 
▽ Highly vulnerable to attack.
en-GB.codex_unit_balloon_faahri_lore_text:
The Supernal transport showcases one of the earliest known uses for Starglass crystal: Igniting the crystal results in a powerful burst of light and heat. Early Faahri used crystals to light their paths through the mountains. 

Like all transport units, the supernal transport bears the traveler's sigil. When on pilgrimage, young Faahri often carry talismans bearing this sigil to protect them from unseen dangers. While this practice has its roots in superstition, mages and seers can actually use the sigil to warn them of natural dangers seconds before impending disaster.
en-GB.codex_unit_balloon_felheim_lore_text: The concoction used to fuel Felheim's Balloons is a foul substance derived predominantly from Fellbat droppings. With the wind behind them, they travel quickly, but their location is often given away by their overpowering odour. Should a Balloon burst, the resulting stench cloud has been known to kill nearby plant life.
en-GB.codex_unit_balloon_floran_lore_text: The Floaty Thing is the Floran Balloon unit. It is powered by a plant found on the bed of the River Bani. When prodded, this plant releases a jet of hydrogen gas to scare off would-be predators. A Floran pilot's primary role is to regularly prod the plant mounted in the Floaty Thing's gondola with a nice, sharp stick.
en-GB.codex_unit_balloon_heavensong_lore_text: Though not particularly hi-tech, a convoy of Heavensong Balloons is a beautiful sight to behold. Each Balloon is constructed like a paper lantern, and glows as it flies. civilian balloons, coloured and decorated, are a common sight in the night sky during festivals and celebrations.
en-GB.codex_unit_balloon_pirates_lore_text:
They were all given a job: Waste as much of the Empire's gold as you can.

None took the assignment so literally as Naron's Balloon Brigade.
en-GB.codex_unit_caravel_cherrystone_lore_text: Heavensong engineers repurposed and sold many of their Riverboats to assist Cherrystone's involvement in the Merfolk-Deepfolk Conflicts. These fine naval craft were key to clearing Deepfolk structures from majority-Merfolk islands in the latter stages of the Conflict.
en-GB.codex_unit_caravel_critical_text:
▲ Highly effective vs. structures
▲ Captures structures
▲ Can enter rivers

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when target is adjacent
    to a structure.
en-GB.codex_unit_caravel_faahri_lore_text:
【Experimental Unit Type-RB】
(from the notes of Pistil Samt-al-Ras)

One of the simpler designs to accomplish! The flame uses the tried and true method of combusting Starglass crystal. 

An aside: recently, the Historical Guild has suggested the humans who previously occupied the Starglass caverns had more uses for Starglass crystal than just light and heat (as we Faahri used them before Enlightenment). 

If only there was more information in the records the humans left behind! Alas, most of their books and papers have been *chewed* through beyond recognition. Why on earth would the humans resort to *eating* their important documents? And why did they have such *tiny* teeth back then? Mysteries I am far too frustrated to consider at the moment.
en-GB.codex_unit_caravel_felheim_lore_text: Lord Valder Ragnarsson produced and delivered fleets of Riverboats as part of his negotiations with the Deepfolk tribes. Though officially, these Riverboats are meant to protect the Deepfolk from further loss of land, some believe the Deepfolk seek to use the boats to reclaim lands allotted to the Merfolk in the treaty of 3006. Only the most absurdly muscular Deepfolk are fit to row in Riverboats, as the design lacks proper fulcra for its oars.
en-GB.codex_unit_caravel_floran_lore_text: Upon witnessing the might of Heavensong Ryuu-boats, Commander Sedge proposed a similar design for the Floran Tribes. Greenfinger Zawan believed the ships would be especially dangerous for the exceptionally flammable Floran, and forbade their construction. Nevertheless, a small fleet of Riverboats was recently discovered near Sedge's army's old encampment. Lacking the seeds that enable the Bloom Dragon's flame, it seems these boats produce fire from whale oil.
en-GB.codex_unit_caravel_heavensong_lore_text:
Based on small sailing vessels from the Kappa clan, Ryuu-boats were invented to help the Empire clear room for saffron farms on overcrowded islands. Though in recent years the Empire has decreased the use of fire-spitting devices in the Saffron Isles, there is yet much work to be done in their newer colonies. A hand-held version of this device was banned in Heavensong shortly before the Empire was permitted to join the International Trade Union.

Heavensong Engineers would use Ryuu-boats as a prototype for what would ultimately become the flying Ryuu battle puppet.
en-GB.codex_unit_caravel_pirates_lore_text:
(Essay excerpt from Nupuri of the Kappa clan)

It is true that some in the Kappa clan have true devotion to Heavensong. But some of us refuse to forget what happened 300 years ago. 

Do you think the Heavensong Dynasty allowed the Kappa to keep our homes in Lake Talon out of kindness or respect? The old King would have taken the whole lake for himself had we not fought and died and wasted so much of his gold. And does no one remember what happened to the poor Tengu clan? The very same that's happening right now to the islands of Saffron! 

I have made contact with a group of Islanders who share the Kappa's fighting spirit. I would not wish the ire of Heavensong on my worst enemy. But if the Islanders are already taking up the fight, I wish to help them.
en-GB.codex_unit_dog_cherrystone_lore_text:
The Battlepup is Cherrystone's Dog unit. These fighting canines are raised from birth by their Battlemasters, with whom their bond is so strong that when their masters are struck down in battle, bereaved pups are relieved from duty and given to their departed Battlemasters' families.

They are fierce and intelligent, and absolutely love bones - a great incentive for fighting the Felheim infantry.
en-GB.codex_unit_dog_critical_text:
▲ Fast and strong, but fragile. 
▲ Best when striking first.
▲ In Fog of War, Scouts see 
  farther than most units, and 
  can see enemies hidden in 
  Forest tiles.

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when another Scout ally 
    is adjacent to the target.
en-GB.codex_unit_dog_faahri_lore_text:
The Pincer Entomon is a marvelous creature with a near-impenetrable orange carapace. 

Pincer entoma shed their carapace thrice per year, becoming vulnerable for the 17 days required for their new exoskeleton to harden. Shedded carapaces have their use in medicine as well as in textiles and architecture as dye and paint. 

Pincer Entoma are not just beloved for their utility--many Faahri choose to care for them as we have observed other cultures caring for canines. Some evidence suggests that pre-Enlightenment Faahri relied on Pincer Entoma for sustenance. If that is the case, we are forever in their debt and do not deserve their companionship.
en-GB.codex_unit_dog_felheim_lore_text:
The Dreadhound is Felheim's Dog unit. The first Dreadhound was raised long ago by a particularly inquisitive Lord of Felheim. Amongst other experiments, the Lord also raised immense skeletal mammoths and fearsome fleshless sharks. Whilst the majority of these experiments failed (the mammoth crumbled under its own weight and the shark sank like a stone), the Dreadhound was a resounding success. Each year there are now almost as many Dreadhounds raised as former humans.

As the saying goes, you can't keep a good dog down.
en-GB.codex_unit_dog_floran_lore_text:
The Quagmutt is the Floran Dog unit. While a Quagmutt is not technically a dog, it's fair to say that the only substantive differences between the two species are the Quagmutt's lack of fur and their absolute refusal to fetch sticks. Otherwise, a Quagmutt is just as good a scout - and just as good a boy - as any other pooch.

These adorable creatures are not bred by the Floran, and are instead found in the Quagmarsh, east of the Floran border. Though entering the Quagmarsh itself is a dangerous endeavour, wild Quagmutts show no aggression towards the Floran who go there to find them (beyond occasionally attempting to cock a leg), and are easily tamed.
en-GB.codex_unit_dog_heavensong_lore_text: The Shiba Inu is Heavensong's Dog unit. Before becoming part of the Heavensong army, Shiba Inu were parade dogs trained for royal ceremonies and entertainment. Despite their new-found role in battle, Shiba Inu still have a place in ceremony today, and as such, know the best show tricks of any battle breed in Aurania. They are bred along the shores of the Cuckoo Oasis and transported to Heavensong's grasslands once they reach adulthood. There, they find the masters they will be paired with for life.
en-GB.codex_unit_dog_pirates_lore_text:
On their way to the beach, Kodjo and his boar companion Nana pass a couple of Heavensong sailors nailing a flyer to a wall.

“WANTED:” the flyer says, “Dread Captain Firebird. Dead or Alive.”

Kodjo can barely stop himself from giggling at how the artist has drawn this ‘Dread Captain’. A body made of smoke. Her face, a skull. Her hair, flames.

The two sailors turn around and demand to know what he's doing. Kodjo stares blankly and cocks his head to one side like a child, pretending he doesn’t understand. The navy makes strange mistakes when they think you are stupid.

On the beach, it takes Nana only a few minutes to find what they’re looking for. The little boar barks happily and begins scratching at the sand. Kodjo helps him dig up a small wooden box filled with treats: Truffles for Nana, and a note inside a glass bottle for Kodjo’s friends in the Governor’s mansion.

Kodjo scans the note, memorizes it, and then feeds that, too, to Nana. Nana looks up at his friend with a pleading face, apparently hungry still.

"What? You want to lick the box?"
en-GB.codex_unit_dragon_cherrystone_lore_text: The Emberwing is Cherrystone's Dragon unit. Professors at the Emberwing Riders' Academy deliver an egg to each new recruit to ensure that their face is the first thing the hatchling sees. The bond formed at the moment of hatching lasts a lifetime, and each Emberwing will ride with no other person thereafter. However, aside from their ability to fly and breathe fire, they're essentially just big dogs.
en-GB.codex_unit_dragon_critical_text:
▲ Deadly. 
▽ Vulnerable to Anti-Air units. 
▽ Can’t attack Air units.
▲ Defend Dragons with Sky
  Riders or other allies!

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when target is on Road.
en-GB.codex_unit_dragon_faahri_lore_text:
The Stygiforme are ill omens--fearsome creatures that make their home in the infinitesimally deep reaches of the Starglass mountains. 

In the early days of Enlightenment, the Stygiforme was a fierce predator of the Faahri. The animosity likely stretches back far into pre-Enlightenment times. In fact, some scholars believe the Stygiforme was responsible for the demise of the humans who once inhabited the Starglass mountain caverns. 

The Stygiforme are incredibly ancient beings. Evidence suggests they are intended to slumber for all of their childhood and adolescence. If this is true, it is possible that whatever work humans were carrying out in Starglass may have awoken the Stygiforme early, making their aggression more of a tantrum caused by an interrupted nap.
en-GB.codex_unit_dragon_felheim_lore_text: The Fellbat is Felheim's Dragon unit. It starts life no bigger than an eagle, but as it matures, it is fed a mixture of carrion and bonemeal derived from fallen Felheim soldiers, causing it to grow to 4 or 5 times its natural adult size. Despite this, the Fellbat is a relatively friendly beast, though clumsy and seemingly unaware of how massive it is.
en-GB.codex_unit_dragon_floran_lore_text: The Bloom Dragon is the Floran Dragon unit. Bloom Dragons are native to the peaks of Rambler's Ruin, just beyond the eastern border of the Floran Lands. Here, they're tended to by Floran Shaman, who feed them seeds prepared by the Greenfinger. The result is a powerful creature capable of drawing power from the sun and unleashing it in a single almighty blast.
en-GB.codex_unit_dragon_heavensong_lore_text:
The Ryuu is Heavensong's Dragon unit. The Heavensong Ryuu MK I is the result of many years of research and development. The frame of the MK I is a masterwork of engineering, emulating the many bones and joints that make up the skeleton of a real dragon. Years were spent assembling and restoring bones found in Dragon's Graveyard as part of the research process. The MK I required the development of new, lighter materials, countless test flights, intense training and a great many late nights. The result is an artificial marvel capable of keeping up with the strongest of airborne beasts.

The soldiers that pilot the Ryuu wear the 'mask of the Dragon' as a mark of... well, piloting a giant dragon.
en-GB.codex_unit_dragon_pirates_lore_text:
The Sky’s children had not been seen in ages. People began to wonder if the Sky’s mother had forsaken the islands and called her children home for good. But Sanka still believed. If he could but find a Skychild, surely it would help them all.

And so, Sanka packed two sacks - one with food and supplies, the other with offerings for the Skychildren - and set off on a journey to climb the peaks of Stonereach island.

On the first day, in scorching heat, Sanka wished for a breeze. A gust of wind blew away his hat, and he had to bear the full might of the sun’s fury. 

On the third day, his skin burnt and peeling, he wished for rain. A midnight flood took his sack of food and carried it into the sea.

On the sixth day - his third without food - Sanka was tempted to eat from the sack of offerings, but stopped himself. How could he face his family and tell them their futures were worth so little to him?

On the ninth day, he reached the summit in an indescribable amount of pain. He stood in the shadow of something tall, cold, and beautiful. He met its gaze, and his face wrenched itself into a teary smile. A skychild! With its power, the islands could be free. Sanka took a step forward, and the world grew dim. Oh, he was so hungry...

...

Sanka awoke under a blanket of palm leaves, with the Sky’s child watching over him. The beast beheld Sanka’s starving frame, and nudged the offering sack toward his hand.

“But... I don’t deserve it. Are you sure?”

As if in answer, the beast set down its head near Sanka's aching legs, and began to fall asleep.
en-GB.codex_unit_frog_cherrystone_lore_text:
Descendants of an early Cherrystone practice, only briefly implemented and long since banned. In lieu of capital punishment, thieves and other criminals could instead choose to serve 10 years of hard Froggitude. But 10 years and hundreds of frogs later, the Cherrystone Witches Council realized they, er… didn't know how to turn them back. 

There are now several vibrant Frogfolk communities along the River Aldor. The most daring among them choose to pursue Knighthood in the service of the crown.
en-GB.codex_unit_frog_critical_text:
▲ Moves on water and land.
▲ Has dangerous Pull ability.

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when target is on Beach
    or River terrain.

  【Pull】 Pulls a non-Commander
  unit one tile closer. (Range: 3)
en-GB.codex_unit_frog_faahri_lore_text:
Records: Pistil Samt-al-Ras

   A strange visitor came by the lab the other day! An amphibian bearing a peculiar letter:

“Dear Faahri, 

Long ago, my clan were once human creatures possessed of thought and word. Alas, our descendants were cursed to live as frogs forevermore. I came from afar seeking the wisdom of Starglass in my clan’s quest to break the curse.”

...Clearly this is some sort of prank. But I *am* in need of test subjects for my next combat unit design…
en-GB.codex_unit_frog_felheim_lore_text:
Of course Cherrystone's magick is too weak to fix their stupid mistake! That's what Pickerel Pumpernyck was thinking as he led his clan from Cherrystone into the frozen wastes of Felheim. They say mages in that wintry land have control over life itself. What better place to turn to for reversing the Frogfolk curse? 

The Pickerel clan never did reclaim the human bodies stolen from their kind—they have no need. Now, with manes of pure moonlight and crowns unburdened by flesh...they found themselves more beautiful than ever.
en-GB.codex_unit_frog_floran_lore_text:
When young Zawan arrived for the day's lesson, Greenfinger Russom was sitting on a rock, caressing the strangest frog Zawan had ever seen. Startled to see the young greenfinger-in-training, the frog lept from Russom's lap and hopped into a nearby bush.

"What was THAT?" Zawan asked.
"A frog," said Russom, unhelpfully. A moment. Then, "There is a leak from below. We must act quickly, while the damage is mild."
en-GB.codex_unit_frog_heavensong_lore_text:
Unsatisfied with the dearth of opportunity afforded their kind in Cherrystone, some Frogfolk communities traveled east to seek their fortunes in Heavensong, that shining dynasty in the desert. They quickly found work pulling heavy objects for farmers, architects, and merchants. 

During a workers' strike, Heavensong engineers developed wind-up automata that could replace the Frogfolk workforce entirely. And so the Frogfolk set off once more.
en-GB.codex_unit_frog_pirates_lore_text:
Izumi thought her life was over, as she stared down the barrel of an Eagle-Eye's rifle. But she would sooner die than give up her comrades now. She braced for the end.

Before the shot rang into the night, Izumi felt a tight squeeze around her torso, and suddenly she was being yanked away… 

When she landed on solid ground, Izumi was face to face with one of the Saffron-pickers from the mainland. Not one of the new machines--a real, live Frog. 

“You saved me…!” 

The Frog bowed its head and turned to leave. Before it could hop away, Izumi called after it. 

"We could give you work! If you're looking for any...." The frog looked at her, cocked its head, and smiled as he answered: 

"Ribbit. Ribbit ribbit.”
".........OK, one croak for yes, two for no."
en-GB.codex_unit_giant_cherrystone_lore_text: The Golem is Cherrystone's Giant unit. Golems are the work of Cherrystone's master stonemasons. They are constructed from the toughest rock washed ashore from Guardian's Teeth, and shaped with tools made of dragon scales. At the heart of each Golem sits a single, pebble-sized Cherrystone, its power imbuing the lifeless stone with sentience and purpose. Those brave enough to place their ear to the Golem's chest may hear strange whispers from within.
en-GB.codex_unit_giant_critical_text:
▲ The most powerful Ground unit.
▲ Easily defeats most units in
  a single hit. 
▲ Incredibly dangerous, even at
  low health.

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when at or below 40
    health.
en-GB.codex_unit_giant_faahri_lore_text:
【Experimental Unit Type-G】
(from the notes of Pistil Samt-al-Ras) 

Happy news. My plans for Experimental Unit Type G were accepted by the new Office of Military Affairs. 

I thought that re-purposing and upgrading mining drills to work similarly to other nations’ "Giant" units was a rather obvious choice, but it seems no one had thought of it before. 

They have offered me a contract to pursue other avenues for bringing our new military up to par with the rest of the world.

I must say, this is not what I imagined for my life. But look on the bright side: The military is offering more funding for this one project than many researchers at the House of Knowledge get for an entire department! I should be happy. I am happy.

I will be happy.
en-GB.codex_unit_giant_felheim_lore_text: The Revenant is Felheim's Giant unit. A Revenant is a living shadow, raised from somewhere beyond death by the combined powers of many Warlocks. Part protection and part prison, the interior of the Revenant's armour is inscribed with ancient wards that form a binding curse, trapping the living shadow inside and dominating its will.
en-GB.codex_unit_giant_floran_lore_text: The Gloom Giant is the Floran Giant unit. It is a creature woven from the roots of the Great Tree that grows at the centre of the Gloomwoods. Armoured with the tree's bark, its kind are considered to be protectors of the Floran Lands. If not called upon to defend their homeland, the Gloom Giants gather around the Great Tree, where they wait silently for years at a time, often allowing the forest's many small creatures to nest upon them.
en-GB.codex_unit_giant_heavensong_lore_text:
The Oni is Heavensong's Giant unit. Though both less advanced and far less agile than Prince Koji's puppet Tenko, Oni MK II battle-puppets use variations of the same technology.

They may appear clumsy and hulking in comparison, but they can deliver an immensely powerful punch. The unarmoured Oni MK I was used solely as a construction device, and is a common sight in Heavensong's ever-growing capital.

The Oni riders wear the 'mask of the ox' as a mark of their power and resilience.
en-GB.codex_unit_giant_pirates_lore_text:
—"Mommy? What did you make me for?"

The Oaracle gave this some thought and answered:

—"Your face; to scare the colonists. Your body, to protect the islanders. Your hands, to strike down all those in your way!"

—"What about after everybody's free?"

—"Hm. After that...whatever makes you happy, darling."

Doug's gaze wanders to the bottles of strange liquids scattered around the Oaracle's workshop. He remembers when he was only a skull on a shelf here, watching in awe as his mother dipped hair-tipped wands into the bottles, and used them to turn blank canvas into magical blurs of color and light. 

—"I think... I wanna paint like Mommy!"

The Oaracle smiles.

—"Then I will need to make you gentler hands."
en-GB.codex_unit_golem_critical_text:
▲ Immensely powerful.
▲ Can attack units in the air.
▽ When deactivated, this unit acts as a neutral structure.
▲ When captured, this unit becomes an ultra-powerful and mobile unit.
▽ Cannot counter-attack.
▽ After attacking, the Guardian must rest for a turn before attacking again.
▲ Regenerates 30 health per turn while resting.
en-GB.codex_unit_griffin_critical_text:
▲ Can fly over enemy lines. 
▽ Attacks from the ground only.
▲ Captures structures.
▲ Strong vs. heavy/wheeled 
  units.

  【Critical Hit】
