    sandwiched between this unit
    and another Air Trooper.
en-GB.codex_unit_griffin_pirates_lore_text:
Jabi smiles calmly at the soldiers approaching his Ostrich farm. "That time of year already?"

Founder's day is nigh, so the search for the Egg of the Emperor has begun.

"Why an *Ostrich* egg, though?" asks the younger soldier.

"Have you seen 'em?! Big as your whole hand. Nothing less for the Empress."

It's said the Emperor's Egg can grant any wish. But it's tradition for the Heavensong Emperor to sacrifice their selfish desires to wish instead for the continued prosperity the Saffron Isles. How fortunate that the wish costs only a few weeks' wages for the Ostrich farmers and the others who facilitate the day's celebrations.

Jabi leads the men to his front porch, where sits this month's haul: a single wooden crate.

"That's ALL?" says the older soldier. "Don't be selfish."
"The girls just ain't layin' a thing these days! Sorry to disappoint."

Truth be told, Jabi sold the last of his birds just the other day, to a woman in a red bandana. The sale had but one condition: "Tell no one." The woman smiled, and raised a finger to her lips. Her skull necklace beamed in the light of the sun like a jeweled egg.
en-GB.codex_unit_harpoonship_cherrystone_lore_: Each Harpoon Ship is armed with bolts that have been tipped with dragon scales and imbued with lightning by Cherrystone's artisan mages. A single bolt weighs upwards of 130 kg, and travels fast enough to catch a Fellbat soaring amongst the clouds.
en-GB.codex_unit_harpoonship_critical_text:
▲ Ranged Naval unit.
▲ Able to attack Air units.
▽ Cannot attack Ground units. 

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when on Reef terrain.
en-GB.codex_unit_harpoonship_faahri_lore_text:
Despite being omnivores, Faahri generally prefer plant-based diets and dislike the taste of fish--which makes the existence of harpoon ships a curious one. 

The Faahri fishing industry is based entirely on the refined palates of our feline animal companions. The animals are picky enough that even gourmet Faahri cuisine cannot sate their appetites--but they *do* generally seem to enjoy fish.
en-GB.codex_unit_harpoonship_felheim_lore_text: The Deepfolk who serve Felheim cover their Harpoon Ships' sharp bolts with bioluminescent algae. When fired at night, the algae disperses in the air, dimly lighting the area for miles around, and exposing the positions of airborne foes.
en-GB.codex_unit_harpoonship_floran_lore_text:
When not at war, the Floran Harpoon Ship, armed with its gigantic bonehead bolt, is used by the Floran to hunt the gigantic beasties of the West Sea. The ships are built to bring down kraken and leviathans, and have proven effective against both.

The Floran that man the Harpoon Ship stay at sea for months at a time, returning home to great esteem and recognition should they succeed in their hunt - and great shame should they fail.
en-GB.codex_unit_harpoonship_heavensong_lore_t: Heavensong's Harpoon ships are armed with powerful glass-tipped bolts, each more expensive than the ship itself. The glass is razor-sharp, produced from the fine sands of Dragon's Graveyard, and can be rigged to shatter before impact, spraying shards into the air at alarming speed.
en-GB.codex_unit_harpoonship_pirates_lore_text:
Mid morning at the port. Odney sits in front of his shack, watching ships come and go. Suddenly, a tall Heavensong officer approaches him.

—"Odney? Is that you?"

Odney nods, tenses, prepares himself for trouble.

—"I'm Kaito! You won't remember me. But when I was young, you took my family on safari to hunt Leaping Fish!"
—"Oh?"
—"That trip changed my life. It's even why I joined the Navy!"

Odney winces.

—"Do you still do safari?"
—"Not today. Lent my boat to some kin a while ago."
—"Pity! I'd take you out on mine, but we're stuck in port for repairs. Ran into pirates last night!"

Kaito motions out to port, where a group of sailors have just pulled a large harpoon from a ship's helm. It must have just missed the helmsman.

Odney whistles. Where did his nephews learn to shoot like that?
en-GB.codex_unit_harpy_cherrystone_lore_text: The Harpy is Cherrystone's Aeronaut unit. Harpies originally came to Cherrystone from across the West Sea, attracted by the scent of the Cinnamon Mines on the west coast. They now make their homes amongst the peaks and slopes above the mines, occasionally aiding hapless miners unfortunate enough to be caught in rockfalls. The Harpies volunteered to join the Cherrystone army to defend the land they have grown to love.
en-GB.codex_unit_harpy_critical_text:
▲ Can attack all unit types.
▲ Good for harrassing enemies
  that can't fight vs. Air.
▽ Watch out for Mages,
  Harpoons, and Ballistas!

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when on Mountain tile.
en-GB.codex_unit_harpy_faahri_lore_text:
【Experimental Unit Type-A】
(from the records of Pistil Samt-al-Ras)

My earlier experiments have revealed that Starglass crystals have different properties depending on their physical state (whole, fragmented, ground, flattened, etc.) These properties can be further altered via the user's intention (such as with Rhabdomancy), though this takes years of practice and can vary wildly. 

The most reliable property of crystals is the release of heat and kinetic energy that occurs when set aflame. I believe we can harness this energy to achieve artificial flight. I have already begun initial designs on a set of crystal-powered wings that should enable Faahri flight engineers to compete with other nations' Aeronauts. 

Nota bene: A strange gaseous substance is released upon burning crystals. I have applied for additional research funding to further study the effects of this gas on health and environment; however, the Faahri Senate would like to produce the prototypes regardless.
en-GB.codex_unit_harpy_felheim_lore_text: The Vampire is Felheim's Aeronaut unit. Historically, Felheim's Vampires have been a scattered and isolated race, unconcerned with the sway of power across Aurania. However, when High Vampire Sigrid joined the legion, the Lesser Vampires flocked to her side, supplying Felheim with a powerful air presence. The Vampires now make their nests in the Crimson Isle, west of the Frozen Forest, united for the first time in centuries.
en-GB.codex_unit_harpy_floran_lore_text: The Leafwing is the Floran Aeronaut unit. Leafwings live in the upper canopy of the Gloomwood. There, they fashion wings from leaves and talons from bone. Their light bodies and natural dexterity make them masters of the air, hunting prey far below, and descending on it with frightening speed. When tracking prey, the Leafwing roam further afield than their grounded kin, and it's not uncommon to spot one as far afield as Cherrystone or Felheim.
en-GB.codex_unit_harpy_heavensong_lore_text:
The Tengu is Heavensong's Aeronaut unit. The men and women of the Tengu clan make their homes on the Pollen Puff Cliffs, just outside Heavensong's southernmost border. Here, where the winds are strong, the Tengu take flight, soaring over Dragon's Cradle on wings of bamboo. They are loyal to Heavensong, relying on the empire for much of their food and trade.

Clan members wear the 'mask of the Tengu' as a mark of their spiritual connection to the heavens.
en-GB.codex_unit_harpy_pirates_lore_text:
Another successful raid! The crew of the Wettbotham were celebrating on deck, laughing and singing songs into the misty night - until, at the end of one song, they heard a faint voice continuing the verse. 

The voice lept higher and higher, louder and louder until the crew were certain it was neither human nor mermish. 

Suddenly, a rush of wind fell upon the deck, sending cold air down the sailor's spines. Before them stood a very tall woman with enormous wings.

After a terror-filled silence, the woman spoke:

"Well, this is a bit awkward, isn't it?" Her voice rang clearly in the sailors' ears, yet her mouth was still. "Sailors are always crashing their ships searching for me. I thought I'd spare you the trouble."

"Your voice is beautiful!" someone stammered.

"Mine? I was thinking the same of yours!"
en-GB.codex_unit_knight_cherrystone_lore_text: The Knight is Cherrystone's Cavalry unit. Cherrystone Knights are men and women of great renown. Though they are masters of many weapons and battle techniques, nothing in a Knight's arsenal is as formidable as their faithful steed. Cherrystone rears its horses on the Greensweep, the range of rolling hills that border Cherry Bay. It is said that the mixture of sea air and pollen blown in from the east gives them their great size and speed.
en-GB.codex_unit_knight_critical_text:
▲ Fast and powerful. 
▲ Deadly vs. footsoldiers.
▽ Watch out for Spear units!

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit after traveling a distance
   of 6 tiles - not simply moving 
   through 6 spaces.

  (Example on next page ⇒)
en-GB.codex_unit_knight_faahri_lore_text:
The cavalry unit's bell produces a sound that has a calming effect on the animal, enabling it to run head-first into danger without fear.

Foreigners reading this guide might wonder: Why ride *Felines* into battle? Canine and Equine animals live near enough that we could THEORETICALLY recruit them into military service. However, these creatures are awful. 

Contrast your lesser 'dogs' or 'horses' to the noble feline: 
  ◆ They do not smell. 
  ◆ They cover their own waste. 
  ◆ They can recall which items and people belong to them without needing to urinate. 

No more need be said.
en-GB.codex_unit_knight_felheim_lore_text: The Dreadknight is Felheim's Cavalry unit. A Dreadknight's steed is a creature of darkness, drawn from across Felheim to its master's side by way of a necrotic blood ritual. The soul of the Dreadknight dominates and absorbs that of its mount until a single consciousness remains. If Dreadknight and stallion are separated for too long, both are driven to a violent madness.
en-GB.codex_unit_knight_floran_lore_text:
The Greenguard is the Floran Cavalry unit. Before Greenfinger Zawan came to power, the fluffalo of the Easterly Glades were little more than a snack to wandering Floran.

However, though they may look chubby and stubby, they have proven to be powerful steeds, and as such are now less likely to be seen merely as dinner. The fluffalo's only form of natural defence is to run head-first into things with its eyes closed - perfect for a Floran charge.
en-GB.codex_unit_knight_heavensong_lore_text: The Tigerlance is Heavensong's Cavalry unit. Tigerlances are creatures of tradition, keepers of old faiths and forgotten secrets in a Heavensong that has long since moved on. Each Tigerlance fashions their lance from dragon bone, believing it to contain the dragon's warrior spirit. The Tigerlance wears the mask of its animal namesake as a mark of the speed, grace and dignity on which they pride themselves.
en-GB.codex_unit_knight_pirates_lore_text:
The movement grows. Zaire thanks the farmer for lending these beasts to the cause - it can't be easy for him, with the Harvest approaching and Heavensong expecting their tax.

Before she can pay the farmer, he hands her a bundle of cloths with holes cut out for eyes.

"Thank you, uncle, but we've already got masks."
"Not for you. For them."

She looks to the donkeys, and back to the farmer, confused.

"Ain't their first ruckus, y'know."

Out of the corner of her eye, Zaire swears she sees a donkey wink at her and grin.
en-GB.codex_unit_kraken_cherrystone_lore_text: As thanks for Cherrystone's aid during the Deepfolk conflicts, the Merfolk gifted some of these creatures to King Mercival II. It is not known what purpose Giant Octopus serve in the unreachable depths of the Merfolk's underwater cities.
en-GB.codex_unit_kraken_critical_text:
▲ High-defence unit.
▲ Can enter River terrain.

 【Critical Hit】
 ★ Crit when target has no
   adjacent allies.

 【Tentacle】 Immobilize any unit for
 one turn. (Range: 3) Kraken takes
 any damage dealt to the tentacle.
en-GB.codex_unit_kraken_faahri_lore_text:
【Experimental Unit Type-K】
(from the records of Pistil Samt-al-Ras)

The best solutions are always the simplest ones. Felines keep breaking ranks to fight with the trained octopuses? Why not invent a metal, crystal-powered cephalopod with fully articulated limbs instead? Pistil, you are a *genius*!
en-GB.codex_unit_kraken_felheim_lore_text:
When alive, these creatures prefer to spend their time deep underwater, and rarely come to the surface. Occasionally, Felheim fishers discover the carcass of one of these creatures washed ashore on an icy beach. 

Baroness Frøygunnr was the first Fell Lord to raise undead Kraken for battle. However, they’ve not been used in more than a century due to the collateral damage they cause.
en-GB.codex_unit_kraken_floran_lore_text:
A rare, highly venomous creature native to the rivers of the Gloomwoods.

After the tragedy of 3045, these creatures were hunted to near-extinction. They of course did not go quietly, claiming dozens of Floran lives in the process. 

Floran Shamans kept a few of these beasts alive to study their venom. To date, no cure has been found, but Shamans identified the next best thing: Removing the venomous sacs from the beasts renders them… well, not *harmless,* but safe enough to handle while training for battle.
en-GB.codex_unit_kraken_heavensong_lore_text:
Once an elusive beast of Kappa clan folklore, a living Korokamu was finally caught by Beautiful Fisherman Ayashi during the Fugōri era of the Heavensong Dynasty. This revolutionized Heavensong cuisine for centuries to come.

Their military usage was unpopular with Heavensong restaurant barons, who already had trouble meeting the demand of hungry customers. As a result, Chief Engineer Mari developed a mechanical version of the beast, pictured here.
en-GB.codex_unit_kraken_pirates_lore_text:
Nadia, Janjak, and Aki gaze into the bay in awe. The day is saved. The Islands are free.

Grandmother Chizoba rushes to the shore to thank the Sea's children for their help - now, and years ago. But just as soon as they came, they vanish into the depths to join their mother.
en-GB.codex_unit_mage_cherrystone_lore_text: The Alchemist is Cherrystone's Mage unit. Alchemists are relatively new to the Cherrystone army, having originally operated as doctors, concocting elixirs and combining them with elemental power in order to cure all manner of maladies. While they still practice medicine on the battlefield, they also use that same magical talent to call down thunder and lightning on their foes.
en-GB.codex_unit_mage_critical_text:
▲ Strong vs. most land units.
▲ Devastating vs. Air units. 
▲ Deadly when attacking from 
  Mountain or Forest tiles.

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when at 3+ tile defence.

  【Heal】 Restore 20 health to
  as many as five allies.
en-GB.codex_unit_mage_faahri_lore_text:
Rhabdomancy was one of the first arts the Faahri learned after Enlightenment, using the divination technique to find safe paths to dig tunnels through the Starglass mountains. 

It is believed that the humans who lived in the mountain's caverns before us were themselves practitioners of experimental Rhabdomancy. According to humans living in the mountain’s foothills, the extinct, cave-dwelling humans were foreign sorcerers from a southern continent. A recently discovered document seems to corroborate this. 

The letter, ravaged by chew marks from our unenlightened ancestors, warns the recipients: 

"You cannot hope to control ----- [...] learn nothing from Requiem? I pray you do not cause a worse ------- than the ---------- worked so hard to end." 

The letter is signed "M------ C-------," and is one of the only surviving records from before Enlightenment.
en-GB.codex_unit_mage_felheim_lore_text: The Warlock is Felheim's Mage unit. Summoned from catacombs deep beneath the Shrieking Wall, it draws its power from the residual necrotic energy in the bones of vanquished allies. The Warlock can often be seen scouring the battlefield after a conflict, snatching up particularly choice skulls and vertebrae with glee. Once the necrotic magic is siphoned from them, they can be ground up and mixed with herbs and oils to form a healing 'Bone Balm'.
en-GB.codex_unit_mage_floran_lore_text: The Shaman is the Floran Mage unit. When it comes to wisdom, the Floran Shaman is considered second only to a tribe's Greenfinger. The Shaman are not only healing herbalists, but are also practised with lightning sorcery, a powerful offensive magic generated by the enchanted red flowers they carry. These flowers grow deep within the Gloomwoods, and their location is a secret known only to the Shaman.
en-GB.codex_unit_mage_heavensong_lore_text: The Thunderbear is Heavensong's Mage unit. In order to wield their lightning rods, they require great strength and swift reflexes. As such, a Thunderbear's regimen consists of a combination of upper body training, balance training and meditation. Only once they reach peak condition can they hope to redirect lightning. They are also able to use their rods to subtly adjust the electrical fields of the body, a process that can heal the injured. The Thunderbear wear the mask of their animal namesake as a mark of their great strength and inner tranquillity.
en-GB.codex_unit_mage_pirates_lore_text:
After the sermon, a child lingers in the pews. The priest knows this child is embarrassed to ask for food or money, so he leaves to sit out on the temple steps. There are but two copper pieces in the donation plate today; the priest hopes the child takes both.

The sun sets. A breeze brushes the priest's face. The child dashes out of the temple and nearly runs headfirst into three skull-faced men walking up the temple steps. The child whispers a flustered apology before bounding down the hill.

The priest knows what these men want; he has denied them several times. What they ask of him, to cast the Storm's Dagger against Heavensong pilots...priests are meant for healing, not cutting others down. Yet as the days wear on, the less he feels that kind deeds alone can cure the islands of their ills. 

Tonight, he will agree to the men's request. After all - surgery is healing, too.
en-GB.codex_unit_merman_cherrystone_lore_text: The Merfolk are Cherrystone's Amphibian unit. Many years ago, King Mercival II brokered a peace between the Merfolk, who inhabit the north side of the Circle Sea, and the Deepfolk of the south. Grateful for this intervention, the Merfolk have been faithful allies of Cherrystone ever since. Though their language is unknown to all but Cherrystone's most learned, one can assume from their 'plip' noises and froggy, toothless smiles that they're rather happy fellows indeed.
en-GB.codex_unit_merman_critical_text:
▲ Can traverse all Land and Sea 
  terrain.
▲ Tip: Attack from the Sea to
  avoid counter-attacks from
  Land units.

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when in River or Sea.
en-GB.codex_unit_merman_faahri_lore_text:
Whereas most nations must recruit merfolk or other species as amphibian soldiers, we have no need. Faahri are excellent swimmers, can tread water for up to three days and hold our breaths for up to an hour before starting to feel ill effects. 

Aquanaut units wear caps of Stigiforme feathers that have been dipped in crystal solution. An aquanaut lost at sea or in the deep watery pools of the mountains can pluck a feather to light their way home.
en-GB.codex_unit_merman_felheim_lore_text: The Deepfolk are Felheim's Amphibian unit. They share an uneasy alliance with Felheim, only recently brokered by Valder. In return for their aid in battle, Valder supplies them with an unending stream of Bone Turtles. Never tiring, and able to survive the deepest of waters, these Turtles have revolutionised Deepfolk trade, agriculture and combat. However, Valder stands ready to turn all of them to dust in an instant should the Deepfolk disobey his command.
en-GB.codex_unit_merman_floran_lore_text: The Splasher is the Floran Amphibian unit. Splashers are native to the Flooded Forest, south of the Floran capital. Here, they have adapted to their watery environment, growing an additional protective layer of algae-like plant matter that produces oxygen when exposed to the sun. Splashers are capable of diving deep beneath the water and staying below the surface for long periods of time. They have even been known to ride the currents into Cherry Bay, much to the shock of Cherrystone's fishermen.
en-GB.codex_unit_merman_heavensong_lore_text:
The Kappa is Heavensong's Amphibian unit. They hail from a small clan that makes its home around Talon Lake, just on the edge of Heavensong's border. The lake serves as both training ground and food source, allowing the Kappa to live independently of Heavensong's wealth. Despite their independence, the Kappa are intensely loyal to Heavensong, and hold Empress Tenri in particularly high regard.

The Heavensong Kappa are rumoured to wear the 'mask of the koi' beneath their helmets as a mark of their aquatic grace, though few outside the clan have ever seen it.
en-GB.codex_unit_merman_pirates_lore_text:
For more than 100 years, we of the Saffron Isles have not been allowed to speak our own language, keep our own customs. The merfolk are the only ones who remember who we used to be.  

When I'm certain my diving helmet is on tight, I nod to Pelipalu. He takes my hand, and together we plunge into the cool water. 

The deeper we go, the harder it is to see until I can see nothing at all. I almost panic. But then I feel us rising once more, and we break surface in a dark underwater grotto.

Pelipalu shouts into the dark and the grotto's crystal walls light up in response. I gasp. 

There is a trading village down here, long abandoned but glittering still. Some of the structures and decorations are clearly mermish, but there is another style too. I do not recognize it with my eyes, but when I see it, my heart cries out in love and agony.

"It's beautiful."
en-GB.codex_unit_rifleman_cherrystone_lore_tex: While training, Marksmen undertake target practice from morning to night, honing their skills in order to become the finest shots Cherrystone has to offer. In addition to this, each individual recruit also works under the tutelage of smiths and artisans to build their own rifle. In this way, they learn the intricacies and idiosyncrasies of the tool upon which their lives and livelihoods rely.
en-GB.codex_unit_rifleman_critical_text:
▲ Deadly—but beware of Dogs!
▽ Strikes only the first foes in
  its line of sight.
▽ Can’t hit foes in Forest or Air.
▽ Must stand still to attack.
▽ Ammo: 3 shots. (Must reload.)

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when target is in centre
    of the Rifleman's sights.
en-GB.codex_unit_rifleman_faahri_lore_text:
【Experimental Unit Type-RM】
(from the records of Pistil Samt-al-Ras) 

There is something seriously wrong about the latest R-Type units. The rifle design is flawless, of course: combustion of the core results in fragmentation of the crystal inside, producing high-energy ionizing radiation from the barrel. It works brilliantly, it's marvelous to behold, and it's among my finest work. However... 

...Possession of one of these weapons has the bizarre effect of making Faahri feel overly self-important. Note the R-Type unit's hat: Unlike other units, such as the Rhabdomancer, this hat serves no purpose. In fact, it likely hinders the ability to conceal oneself properly in a sniper's nest. The hat's only utility is to enable the obnoxious behavior of bragging about the size of one's hat. 

Alas, we ship out to Aurania in just two weeks. There is nothing to be done but pray the enemy can knock some sense into them.
en-GB.codex_unit_rifleman_felheim_lore_text: Initial teething problems in Felheim’s Dreadeye programme included fractured clavicles, displaced humeri, dislodged skulls and, in the severe case of one Private Ivar, full skeletal fragmentation. However, now that sufficient padding has been added to these marksmen’s tunics in order to absorb the full shock of rifle kickback, the programme is really finding its feet. Unlike Private Ivar.
en-GB.codex_unit_rifleman_floran_lore_text: In your mind’s eye, picture a tree, hedge or patch of grass. Now, picture that same tree, hedge or patch of grass with a Floran Sniper in it. Take careful note of any visual differences that may occur between the first and the second mental picture. In what ways did the tree, hedge, or patch of grass change over the course of your imaginings? If your answer to this question is, "No change was visible", then you have correctly completed this exercise. If a Floran Sniper is hiding in the brush, you will not see them...
en-GB.codex_unit_rifleman_heavensong_lore_text:
Like their avian namesake, the Eagle-Eyes are peerless hunters. Their training is rigorous and unforgiving - only the most skilled marksmen are allowed to train for the position, and only a small percentage of those individuals successfully graduate. Recruits hone their skills in patience and observation as well as accuracy to the point where they seldom miss their target. 

They wear the mask of the eagle as a mark of their excellence.
en-GB.codex_unit_rifleman_pirates_lore_text:
A shooting range. A dozen men crowd around the youngest, teaching all they know.

—"Ye hafta trust the bird. *Believe* in the bird. She's got better eyesight; yours'll just get in the way."

The new recruit is horrified. "So you gouge out your own *eyes*?"

—"What! 'Course not. These are *blindfolds*, not eye-patches!" 

All the musketeers laugh and remove their coverings, revealing eyes that are perfectly intact. All, except Wilky.

— "...So nobody else went through with it?"
en-GB.codex_unit_soldier_cherrystone_lore_text:
The Swordsman is Cherrystone's Soldier unit. Loyal and true, the Swordsman has been the bedrock of the Cherrystone army for many years. Swordsmen fight for their love of Cherrystone and its Queen. Though they are the most numerous of all units, each and every Swordsman has their name etched upon the walls of the hall of remembrance deep inside Cherrystone Castle.

When not in battle, the Swordsman can be observed engaged in such activities as rescuing cats stuck in trees and hosting bingo tournaments for the Cherrystone mages.
en-GB.codex_unit_soldier_critical_text:
▲ Most basic combat unit. 
▲ Cost-effective for capturing 
  structures and body-blocking. 
▽ Vulnerable to most units.

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when beside an allied
    Commander.
en-GB.codex_unit_soldier_faahri_lore_text:
Do not be misled by the Faahri swordhand’s low recruit cost. Everything in our society requires excellence, and our duelists are no exception. 

Like most Faahri weapons, the Duelists' rapiers are refined metal enhanced with fragments of Starglass crystal. 

A duelist's shield bears the stone sigil, which represents strength and protection. The symbol resembles a simple rhomboid when viewed from afar.
en-GB.codex_unit_soldier_felheim_lore_text:
The Dreadsword is Felheim's Soldier unit. Though poorly armed with rusted swords and splintered shields, the sheer rate at which Felheim is able to produce Dreadswords makes them a fearsome foe. The clatter of bones and the chatter of teeth foretells their coming as they swarm tirelessly over mountain and forest.

During peacetime, the Dreadsword may turn their attention to pursuits they valued in life. Indeed, it is not uncommon to spot a Dreadsword painting, whittling or ice fishing among the desolate wastes of Felheim.
en-GB.codex_unit_soldier_floran_lore_text:
The Slasher is the Floran Soldier unit. Though the Floran are lithe and beautiful, moving with other-worldly grace and agility, they also display terrifying aggression and a keen hunter's instinct. The Floran Slasher epitomises this dichotomy. Armed with only jagged bone swords, claws and fangs, their savagery is unmatched.

An army of Floran Slashers on the march resembles a breeze rustling through a field of grass.
en-GB.codex_unit_soldier_heavensong_lore_text:
The Lionblade is Heavensong's Soldier unit. The Lionblades are elite footsoldiers trained for many years in the Gilded Desert. The harsh sun and burning sand make for brutal conditions, and many recruits fail to reach the end of their training.

Fully trained Lionblades wear the 'mask of the lion', a priceless mark of their ferocity shaped from solid gold by Heavensong's expert artisans. It is said that Heavensong's armies march sporting enough gold to purchase a kingdom.
en-GB.codex_unit_soldier_pirates_lore_text:
He meets Janjak at the teahouse, their usual spot when the day's labour is done. 

Janjak sets down a heavy burlap toolsack, takes a big drink, and stares out the window as the setting sun paints golden the bare arm of the island reaching into the bay.
» "All this was ours, once."

Something is different with him today.

Janjak nods to the burlap sack under the table. Ronil watches as he opens its flap, revealing a glint of sharp metal--a cutlass? And beneath it, a black helmet with a carved ivory skull. 

Ronil's eyes widen as his friend leans in and lowers his voice.

» "Ours once, and ours once more."
en-GB.codex_unit_spearman_cherrystone_lore_tex: The Pikeman is Cherrystone's Spearman unit. Once fully trained, each and every Cherrystone Pikeman is taken to the sacred Sage Woods in eastern Cherrystone. Here, they're taught to harvest wood from ancient trees and craft the spears they will take into battle. When not in combat, they maintain the woods, nurturing the trees for future generations.
en-GB.codex_unit_spearman_critical_text:
▲ Slow but powerful, with strong
  defence. 
▲ Useful for wall formations and
  attacking structures.
▲ Super effective vs. Cavalry.

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when adjacent to an
    allied Spearman.
en-GB.codex_unit_spearman_faahri_lore_text: Written on the outer rim of the Perforator's helmet is the focus sigil, a reminder of the unit’s precision and power. Exceptional Perforators have such fine control over their weapon that they can pierce a hole into Starglass crystal without shattering it.
en-GB.codex_unit_spearman_felheim_lore_text: The Dreadspear is Felheim's Spearman unit. Once raised, Dreadspears are sent to scavenge deep within the Frozen Forest. The forest serves as a graveyard of sorts for the many large beasts that roam Felheim's icy expanses. The Dreadspears look for bones among the snow that might be fashioned into jagged spears.
en-GB.codex_unit_spearman_floran_lore_text: The Stabber is the Floran Spearman unit. Beginning as saplings, Floran Stabbers craft a spear from the bones of each beast they successfully hunt. Ever on the prowl for bigger and more fearsome quarry, Stabbers must craft their 10th spear before they are accepted into the Floran army. Stabbers often decorate their spears with the leaves and flowers they lose whilst hunting a foe.
en-GB.codex_unit_spearman_heavensong_lore_text:
The Heronguard is Heavensong's Spearman unit. The Heronguard are trained on the Scorched Beach, where they're taught to spear lightning-fast sailfish without disturbing the water. They are almost as dangerous with the butt of their spears as they are with their points.

The Heronguard wear the mask of their avian namesake as a mark of their speed and grace.
en-GB.codex_unit_spearman_pirates_lore_text:
When Masako finishes her Colonial guard duty for the day, she sneaks off to Serpent Islet, to fish with Roseline and her family. Masako's Heavensong spear and training is no match for the nimble fish of the islands--but Roseline never makes fun of her. 

Roseline's family are all so kind and lovely that Masako feels like she's part of it. Today, Masako trembles, because she will ask to join the family officially. Today, Masako will tell Rosaline that she alone has her heart.

When Masako reaches Roseline's house, her stomach turns. Roseline's family is outside with all their belongings, and the door to their home bears the Heavensong seal, marking it as confiscated property of the Empire.

Masako saves her confession for another day, and instead makes a promise: that she will do whatever's necessary to protect Roseline, her family, her islands.

The next morning, Masako was missing from her regiment's role call. Also missing: 70 sets of Heavensong helmets, masks, and polearms.
en-GB.codex_unit_thief_cherrystone_lore_text: The roguish Lightfingers learn their trade at the Silver Tower Academy, situated deep within Cherrystone’s northern woods. They are trained in athletics, acrobatics, espionage, counter-espionage, counter-counter-espionage, sneaking, skulking and thieving. Graduates either join Cherrystone’s Guild of Lightfingers or abscond to a life of secrecy and shadows.
en-GB.codex_unit_thief_critical_text:
▲ Instantly neutralizes enemy
  structures. 
▽ Vulnerable. Cannot attack.
▽ Slower when carrying loot.

▶ 【Ransack】 Loot a structure.
  Thief must Deposit money at
  Hideout to use.
▶ 【Bypass】 Slip past Gates
  without first destroying them.
en-GB.codex_unit_thief_faahri_lore_text:
Thievery: an art that was commonly practiced by our unenlightened ancestors, before the Faahri Republic came to be. It is believed that in the Age of Empty Thoughts, entire families of Faahri could live undetected in the dwellings of more powerful creatures, subsisting on stolen scraps of food and making homes out of stolen textiles and paper. 

Wanton thievery is uncivilised behaviour. But if our contemporaries use thieves in clandestine military operations, then so must we.'
en-GB.codex_unit_thief_felheim_lore_text: The hard, white bone of the Prowler’s skeletal face belies its incorporeal nature. Behind its mask, and beneath its tattered robes, its form is shadowy and spectral. These wan and ghostly individuals can slip in and out of buildings with ease, moving with otherworldly silence and stealth.
en-GB.codex_unit_thief_floran_lore_text: The Floran are natural-grown hunters, excellent at stalking their prey. The Sneakers are the stealthiest and slyest stalkers of them all. Once a Floran who may possess the skills to become a Sneaker is identified, the individual in question is given an aptitude test. The test is very straightforward - a polished coin of any denomination is held up, and the subject is asked, "On a scale of one to ten, how much do you want this very shiny object?" If the answer is ten or above, the individual in question qualifies to train as one of these elite operatives.
en-GB.codex_unit_thief_heavensong_lore_text:
So stealthy and agile are the Fleetfoot that their abilities seem almost supernatural. For this reason, many outside of Heavensong believe them to have the magical abilities of flight and invisibility. This is even the official (albeit mistaken) opinion of certain foreign governments. 

The Fleetfoot wear the mask of the hare as a mark of their nimble swiftness.
en-GB.codex_unit_thief_pirates_lore_text:
The way the Empire presented itself to the world, you’d think every citizen was rich. Not so. Not Izumi. By the time she was of age, she’d inherited enough debt to last a lifetime.

Izumi had heard there were cushy jobs in Saffron that paid handsomely–but she didn’t realize you had to *know* someone with a cushy job to *get* one. The wages Izumi made cleaning offices and mess halls in the naval base could hardly lift one of her *fingers* out of poverty. 

Yet just out of reach, in all of the offices she cleaned was gold. Loads of it. Right there, teasing her. The empress would hardly miss just a few coins…

…And that was how Izumi wound up in an imperial jailhouse. She’d been there weeks, with not even an estimate of when her trial would be. As she sulks in the corner of her cell, a guard stops by.

“Saw your name in the paper,” says the guard. “Ten thousand gold pieces, huh?”

Izumi buries her head in shame.

“As luck’d have it, there’s a project going on that could use someone with your skills… If you’ll join us, ask for water around sunset tomorrow.” 

Izumi thought about it the whole night. It wasn’t gold she wanted, really. Whether in a jail cell, or the naval base, or back home in the slums of Hinmin town, Izumi saw herself trapped inside an hourglass. She could only watch the beauty of the outside world, and scream as her own world slowly filled with sand.

In the morning, Izumi woke with a scratch in her throat. 

Water. She needed water.
en-GB.codex_unit_travelboat_cherrystone_lore_t:
During peacetime, these Barges are used to trade goods with Heavensong. It's not uncommon to see children waiting at the docks to sing a song to the Merfolk onboard, hoping they might share some of their cargo.

''Ello Mister, how do ye do? Plip plip, plip plip.
Where have you been travellin' to? Plip plip, plip plip.
Did you bring back somethin' nice? Plip plip, plip plip.
Silk and spices, herbs and rice? Plip plip plip!

Once in a while, the Merfolk hand out brightly coloured exotic seashells found on the Scorched Beach and the children are left daydreaming of lands far away.
en-GB.codex_unit_travelboat_critical_text:
▲ Transports up to two units 
  that would otherwise travel
  on land.
▽ Units must be on Beach tile to
  board the Barge.
▽ When this unit is defeated,
  all loaded units are lost.
▲ Can cross Rivers and Bridges.
▽ Highly vulnerable.
en-GB.codex_unit_travelboat_faahri_lore_text:
For most young Faahri, thalassic transports are symbols of freedom: Most pilgrimages begin at the human port towns south and west of the mountains. 

Due to its reputation for hostility, incivility, and barbarism, Aurania is an extremely unpopular Pilgrimage destination. Nevertheless, every few years some Faahri child will give into baser curiosity and spend their precious time in Aurania, hiding amongst the clueless Cherrystoners, exploring the rancid Felheim wastes, etc. Rarely has this ever been worth the trouble--though we do have former President Radius' pilgrimage to thank for our country's current relationship with the wise and enduring Heavensong Empire.
en-GB.codex_unit_travelboat_felheim_lore_text: It takes particularly brave Deepfolk to pilot a Barge full of undead cargo. Those with experience, however, will know that once a Barge reaches open sea, the rocking motion of the waves tends to send the undead to sleep. With no nose to snore through, they rest in eerie silence, dreaming the dreams they had in life.
en-GB.codex_unit_travelboat_floran_lore_text: The Floran Barge is a simple vessel, poorly constructed and partially reclaimed from coastal wreckage. No one is really sure why it floats... it probably shouldn't float, but it does... Heedless and gutsy, the Floran are all too happy to pile into one and take to the open sea. It's unclear if the wheel at the front of the vessel is actually attached to anything, but turning it seems to make the captain happy.
en-GB.codex_unit_travelboat_heavensong_lore_te: Heavensong's fleet of Barges were originally built as trade vessels, importing and exporting goods from lands both near and far. Each Barge is beautifully constructed and able to remain at sea for months at a time, facilitating trade with peoples beyond Aurania. Since being commissioned for war, their hulls have been strengthened and their capacity has been increased.
en-GB.codex_unit_travelboat_pirates_lore_text:
Far, far away from Aurania and the Saffron Islands, a ship with black sails makes port. An official-looking woman - the city's treasurer - glances at the ship, and motions for Zidane and his crew to unload their cargo: Dozens of chests full of the Heavensong Empire's coin. 

There is no way to know if this country will keep their word, support the Islands after Liberation Day - but Zidane has to believe. He watches as the last of the gold vanishes into the Treasurer's wagons to be melted and re-minted in another leader's image.

Zidane hopes there will be some gold left for the *islanders,* when everything's through.
en-GB.codex_unit_trebuchet_cherrystone_lore_te: Being a weapon primarily of siege warfare, it has been many centuries since Cherrystone has had any need of the Trebuchet. In fact, at the time of writing, there are only 6 remaining in commission, their wood creaking and their ropes weary. Despite this, the knowledge of their construction has been carefully preserved, and soldiers are trained in Trebuchet operation as a matter of course.
en-GB.codex_unit_trebuchet_critical_text:
▲ Devastating long-range unit. 
▲ Useful for controlling key 
  battlefield space. 
▽ Can’t move and attack on the
  same turn.

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when target is at max.
    attack range.
en-GB.codex_unit_trebuchet_faahri_lore_text: Only the finest projectile-motion calculators are able to operate parabolic projectile launchers. The result is a highly accurate and utterly devastating siege weapon.
en-GB.codex_unit_trebuchet_felheim_lore_text: The Trebuchet is a recent addition to the legion, reflecting the degree to which Valder has brought structure and organisation to Felheim. Though its operators are unpractised and unruly, it has proved an effective addition to Felheim's armies.
en-GB.codex_unit_trebuchet_floran_lore_text: The Treebuchet is the Floran Trebuchet unit. It is constructed almost entirely from living wood taken from the Great Tree at the centre of the Gloomwoods. The Treebuchet is considered to be alive, and as such, is treated with great respect by the Floran. In fact, technically, it outranks those who operate it.
en-GB.codex_unit_trebuchet_heavensong_lore_tex: Heavensong's Trebuchets launch projectiles made up of a brittle eggshell-like casing, usually filled with potent gunpowder. These projectiles explode on impact, with devastating effect. On occasion, Commanders have seen fit to fill the shells with alternative payloads, ranging from caltrops to flaming pitch, and on one unusual occasion, cabbages.
en-GB.codex_unit_trebuchet_pirates_lore_text:
“Ready!”
“Steady!”
“FIRE!”

The three soldiers watched breathless as the payload went soaring over the navymen’s heads and into the side of the imperial auction house. They were a unit. They were crew. They were family. They moved as one, and their speed and accuracy was to be feared by all.
en-GB.codex_unit_turtle_cherrystone_lore_text: The Sea Turtle is Cherrystone's Turtle unit. Sea Turtles are considered by Merfolk to be the horses of the sea (... they haven't heard of seahorses). Their shells are treated with a rare type of red seaweed before being left to dry in the sun. Once dry, they harden, becoming near-impenetrable, and gaining their distinct crimson hue in the process. The Merfolk continue to refine and cultivate the seaweed, which also makes for a fine lunch.
en-GB.codex_unit_turtle_critical_text:
▲ Fast and powerful.
▲ Can cross enemy lines.
▲ Useful for rushing units with
  a large attack range.

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit from Deep Sea terrain.
en-GB.codex_unit_turtle_faahri_lore_text:
【Experimental Unit Type-T】
(from the records of Pistil Samt-al-Ras)

Many nations use various species of reptile for naval warfare. The species nearest to Starglass have softer shells than most others. As I am charged with bringing the Faahri army up to par with the rest of the world, this simply will not do. Perhaps if we reinforced their shells with the shedded carapaces of the Pincer Entoma...
en-GB.codex_unit_turtle_felheim_lore_text: The Bone Turtle is Felheim's Turtle unit. These fearsome creatures were raised by Valder and gifted to the Deepfolk in return for their naval support. With bones almost as hard as their robust shells, they make for a formidable maritime threat. The Deepfolk sharpen their Turtles' beaks with whetstones, turning them into fierce weapons capable of rending the hull of even the sturdiest of vessels.
en-GB.codex_unit_turtle_floran_lore_text: The Mudsnapper is the Floran Turtle unit. It is a strange creature, found in the waters of the Flooded Forest. Its skin has a porous, soil-like quality, and plant life often grows directly on its body. Mudsnappers are easy to train, and the Splashers of the Flooded Forest have been riding their soft and springy shells for many years.
en-GB.codex_unit_turtle_heavensong_lore_text: The Cogshell is Heavensong's Turtle unit. Though otherwise entirely constructed from wood, its shell is salvaged from the remains of an actual turtle, before being covered with gold leaf and decorative etchings. Its movement is powered by two mechanical waterwheels that can run both backwards and forwards, providing great speed and agility.
en-GB.codex_unit_turtle_pirates_lore_text:
As we explore the ruins of the underwater trading village, we hear splashing in the water where we entered. Someone else is down here. 

I have been with the liberation movement so long my mind immediately turns to Heavensong. Could they have followed us? Weaponless, I look around for options. Pelipalu readies his trident. More splashing. Are we being ambushed? How many are there?

I soon get my answer: Eight. Three adult spined turtles, and five children. The adults are fierce when they want to be--but they seem to understand we mean them no harm. A thought occurs to me.

"Pelipalu," I say, "Have you ever tried *riding* one of these?"
en-GB.codex_unit_villager_cherrystone_lore_tex: The denizens of Cherrystone are a settled people, having long lived in peace with full and thankful hearts. Cherrystone's royal family supplies each of the kingdom's villages with well-travelled scholars to provide free education, and in turn, these villages produce some of the best farmers and artisans known to Aurania.
en-GB.codex_unit_villager_critical_text:
▼ Unable to attack. 
▼ However,
▼ If you can convince your
  troops that this unit is 
  dangerous, 
▼ If you can make your soldiers
  see weapons in empty hands, 
▼ You can get away
  with all sorts of things.
en-GB.codex_unit_villager_faahri_lore_text:
Attached is the style of dress typical of male Faahri scribes and scholars, as well as young Faahri embarking on their pilgrimage. 

All Faahri are required to take part in a knowledge pilgrimage at least once in their life: a year-long period of travel where they learn more about the world and record their knowledge for the betterment of Faahri society.

Upon returning, each pilgrim presents their travelogue to the Erudite Eight for consideration to be inducted into the House of Knowledge. Many Faahri dream of helping their society achieve its ultimate destiny by adding knowledge to the House's halls.
en-GB.codex_unit_villager_felheim_lore_text: Look beyond the fearsome visage and alarming chatter, and you'll find Felheim's undead peasant folk to be a quaint and kind lot, eking out a life amongst the frozen wastes. Come winter solstice, many Villagers trek to Silentstone, where they deliver knitted scarves and jackets to the undead veterans at rest there.
en-GB.codex_unit_villager_floran_lore_text:
Floran civilians are a boisterous bunch, just barely under the control of the tribe's Greenfinger. Floran culture revolves around hunting, sneaking and sneaky hunting, with the best hunters occupying the most coveted positions in society.

Whilst the Floran can be a frightening people, they're also fiercely loyal. After studying Floran society, Doctor Remus Ambustus, an anthropologist from Cherrystone, was quoted as saying 'The Floran have become my best friends. Never have I trusted a group of people more implicitly', before suddenly disappearing.
en-GB.codex_unit_villager_heavensong_lore_text: The citizens of Heavensong are a thoughtful and creative people, their day to day lives demonstrating a harmony of technology and tradition. Together, science and spirituality form the lifeblood of Heavensong's wealth, trade, might and culture. Heavensong's greatest artists and architects are celebrated for their ingenuity, whilst science and invention are considered art forms in and of themselves.
en-GB.codex_unit_villager_pirates_lore_text:
The hardest of these tales to record is my own. Not because it's exceptional.

I was a stagehand at the Shining Shell Theatre. Before it shut down, an actress asked me if I had any work lined up. Her name was Nadia. Simple as that.

No, it's difficult because I know I don't *have* to be here, like most of the others. I know if I saved enough money, I could purchase travel fare and move to the Mainland. If I kept my head down, I could find work on some lord's estate and be mistaken for a man of pure Heavensong lineage who spends too much time in the sun. I have no debts. I could be all but guaranteed a long life, if an uneventful one.

I also know the sands would feel rough on my feet. The booming hum of the desert's dunes would keep me up at night. I would feel lonely without the ocean's song at my window.

Still, it would be nice to visit the Mainland without getting awful looks. To not feel like a stranger in my mother's birthplace.

- Aki Isiaka-Isaka
en-GB.codex_unit_wagon_cherrystone_lore_text: Cherrystone Wagons were originally built to transport goods to market. Though long since reassigned, it's not uncommon for a band of soldiers to emerge from one with the faint smell of cinnamon buns clinging to their clothing.
en-GB.codex_unit_wagon_critical_text:
▲ Transports units across long
  distances. (Faster by Road.)
▲ Carries any footsoldier, Dog,
  or Air Trooper.
▽ When this unit is defeated,
  any unit it carries is lost.
▽ Cannot traverse Mountain or
  Forest tiles.
en-GB.codex_unit_wagon_faahri_lore_text:
Terranean transport vehicles are adorned with the Knot of the Traveler, for safe passage in unfamiliar lands.

Starglass’ native feline animals are remarkably strong. A single feline can comfortably pull 150x its own weight; however, sometimes it will refuse to do so for absolutely no good reason. 

Though not much is known about the pre-Enlightenment relationship between our ancestors and felines, today they are a much beloved animal companion. Many wagon-drivers see felines as part of their natural-born family. What good fortune, then, that Faahri and our felines share a similar average lifespan of about 30 years.
en-GB.codex_unit_wagon_felheim_lore_text: Though small, Felheim's Wagons are capable of transporting a surprising number of footsoldiers by means of an ingenious method that involves disassembling them and laying their bones in neat rows. In an effort to avoid bone-ownership disputes, most have taken to engraving small emblems into their skeletons that serve as name tags, and some even add reassembly instructions.
en-GB.codex_unit_wagon_floran_lore_text: The bed of a Floran Wagon is covered in soil that houses the roots of the gigantic plants that form the Wagon's canopy. As with much of the plant life used in Floran construction and armour, the leaves are remarkably strong, and regenerate at an astonishing speed. The Wagon is pulled along by a friendly fluffalo, commonly found in the Easterly Glades.
en-GB.codex_unit_wagon_heavensong_lore_text: Driven by monkey-masked footsoldiers, Heavensong's Wagons are masterfully constructed, and require very little horsepower despite their large frames. Heavensong's Prince Koji speaks often of a future with horseless Wagons capable of travelling vast distances, though his advisors consider this little more than a childish dream.
en-GB.codex_unit_wagon_pirates_lore_text:
Today, Bariki Island was seized for “imperial economic development,” which everyone knew meant either a resort or a saffron plantation. Because Tamara would not leave peacefully, they took her by wagon.

She'd felt brave in the moment, but in the back of the Heavensong wagon, dread overcomes her. No one knew what colonial prisons were like - people rarely ever came back. 

The wagon driver's voice interrupts Tamara's thought spiral. "When we stop, take my seat," he says. "Don't worry about steering. The donkey knows the way." 

Suddenly, the wagon veers off the road. The carriage bounces, threatens to tip over - but they came to a safe stop at the edge of a small forest where, sure enough, a donkey is tied to a tree, draped in black cloth.

The driver cuts Tamara loose from her bindings, unties the donkey, and exchanges it with his horse. He rips the Heavensong banners from the wagon and replaces it with the donkey's cloth. Finally, he mounts his horse and prepares to leave. Tamara notices that he's forgotten a small pouch of gold in the driver's seat.

"Why are you doing this?" Tamara asks. The driver says nothing. He bows his head to her, and speeds away on the horse.

Tamara isn't sure what's going on - but she will absolutely spend all of this man's gold.
en-GB.codex_unit_warship_cherrystone_lore_text: Whilst Cherrystone's Warships are built at home by skilled shipwrights, they're manned by Merfolk from the Circle Sea. So attuned are the Merfolk to the movements of the sea that they're able to send their ships dancing amongst the waves with eerie grace.
en-GB.codex_unit_warship_critical_text:
▲ Most powerful Naval unit.
▲ Travels fast, has long-range
  attacks.
▲ Can move and attack on the
  same turn.
▽ Cannot attack Naval units. 

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when on Beach terrain.
en-GB.codex_unit_warship_faahri_lore_text:
【Experimental Unit Type-W】
(from the records of Pistil Samt-al-Ras) 

Failure. Shame. Defeat. I had meant for the Type-W unit to be capable of far more devastation than other nations' warships. Yet, no matter which methods I employ, I am unable to draw more power from Starglass crystals than you would get with a mere cannonball. In fact, ALL of the weapons I have created are merely on par with every other nation's. 

I know MUCH more power resides within our crystals. Flames produced by igniting Starglass crystal *never* burn out naturally. Skilled Rhabdomancers and Hexologists use the crystals to summon incredible bursts of power that I cannot reproduce in the lab. 

There must be some secret to this. But will I ever discover it? After all, I am nearly 26, practically 30. I can only hope... 

No. Not hope. I *will* do it. 

And because I have willed it, it will be so.
en-GB.codex_unit_warship_felheim_lore_text: Felheim's Warships are built and manned by Deepfolk from the Circle Sea. The Deepfolk harvest wood from the coast of Dragon's Cradle, hauling it into the water and constructing the ships in the ocean itself. The Deepfolk possess a bioluminescent stalk, and at night, the decks of Felheim Warships seem alive with ghostly lights.
en-GB.codex_unit_warship_floran_lore_text: The Floran build their Warships from the remains of pirate ships that wash up on Plunderer's Coast, patching up their hulls with clumps of moss and vines. They are manned by large crews of boisterous Floran, who clamber nimbly around the decks, somehow managing to manoeuvre them as if they were far more seaworthy vessels.
en-GB.codex_unit_warship_heavensong_lore_text: Superior technology has long made Heavensong's naval force the most dominant in Aurania. Heavensong Warships are strong, fast, sturdy and so simple to control that only a small crew is required. Just a single gunner can man all three of the Warship's forward cannons.
en-GB.codex_unit_warship_pirates_lore_text:
『Captain’s Log』
Nupuri of the Kappa Clan

This ship will be my grave. And yet I go gladly, having given my life to protect others.

To Yuppo... I’m only strong now because of big brother. Thank you for everything. I go to pierce the sky.

To Pirika... I’m an idiot for not taking you to the moon festival last year. Maybe next time. 

To little Noichu... the
en-GB.codex_unit_witch_cherrystone_lore_text: The Witch is Cherrystone's Sky Rider unit. Both male and female Witches are trained deep within the Sage Woods. There, they learn to commune with the spirits of the wood, friendly and sleepy little creatures connected to the power of the land. It is through their interactions with these creatures that Witches learn to harness some of that power. Each Witch takes a tiny spirit, invisible to the untrained eye, as their companion, often storing it in a warm pocket amongst their robes. Witches fight to protect their people and the land they hold dear, and only use martial spells in times of war.
en-GB.codex_unit_witch_critical_text:
▽ Attacks Air units only. 
▽ Less powerful when target is 
  beside an allied Sky Rider.

  【Critical Hit】
  ★ Crit when target has no
  adjacent Sky Rider ally.
   
  【Hex】 Deal 10 damage to all
  enemies in a 4-tile radius.
en-GB.codex_unit_witch_faahri_lore_text:
【Experimental Unit Type-SR】
(from the records of Pistil Samt-al-Ras) 

In my latest double-blind experiment, 84 percent of expert Hexologists found my crystal-powered broomsticks easier to use and more forgiving than traditional broomsticks. 

Most shockingly, when crystal-powered broomsticks were given to complete novices, 77 percent were able to achieve flight within 3 days. (Decagon et al. found that novices take an average of 180 days to achieve flight with traditional brooms.) 

Furthermore, 81 percent of all crystal-powered broom users rated the padded seats as "very comfortable," while 99 percent of traditional broom users had to pause their interview at some point to remove splinters from their buttocks.
en-GB.codex_unit_witch_felheim_lore_text: The Wraith is Felheim's Sky Rider unit. It is born of the undead remnants of a necromancer. Though the Wraith can no longer control its necrotic powers, its bones burn with the grim magic it absorbed in life. In battle, the Wraith reaches out with all its malice and willpower, and sends stored magic soaring in a rushing bolt to strike its foes. Less forceful, though perhaps more insidious, are its Hexes. These miasmic spells are given substance by the Wraith's deep-seated spite.
en-GB.codex_unit_witch_floran_lore_text: The Swooper is the Floran Sky Rider unit. Floran Swoopers are students of the Shaman, and ingest the enchanted red flowers the Shaman grow in order to gain their aerial abilities. Swoopers are capable of both flight and lightning sorcery, a combination of skills that allows them to dominate the air. Each Swooper carries a pouch of the Shamanic red flowers' powdered roots, which they can disperse over surrounding enemies to cause them minor harm - the Floran version of a 'Hex'. Swoopers are strangely serene in comparison to other Floran, perhaps as a side effect of consuming these flowers.
en-GB.codex_unit_witch_heavensong_lore_text:
The Stormowl is Heavensong's Sky Rider unit. Though they wield smaller and less powerful lightning rods than their Thunderbear counterparts, their training is similar and just as rigorous. The Stormowls are a new addition to Heavensong's forces, with flying staves of Prince Koji's own design, first built just two short years ago. When in flight, they are able to harness the natural atmospheric electricity that surrounds us to force a low-level negative charge through the air. This 'Hex' is nebulous, and disperses over a wide area.

The Stormowl wears the mask of its avian namesake as a mark of its balance in all things.
en-GB.codex_unit_witch_pirates_lore_text:
Magic is forbidden in Heavensong. Therefore, magic is forbidden in the Saffron Isles--at least, in theory. The Empire typically doesn't waste its time interfering with old folk magic, as long as it's kept behind doors. That's why Yendi was surprised to see dozens of Heavensong navymen heading straight for her Artist's Retreat. They tore through canvases, confiscated enchanted paintbrushes, destroyed the haunted kilns, and took Yendi away in chains.

Months later, as Yendi faced the gallows, a breeze touched her face. She closed her eyes a moment to savour the wind's kiss. When she opened them, the executioner was staring pale-faced at the sky. Above, hundreds of hooded figures were swarming, uttering curses in a language no one remembered. Yendi's disciples--her muses--had come to her rescue.

And the wind began to roar.
